question: Question: which passing test cannot fail? Statically audit every test for: no assertion at all; an assertion on a literal; assert True; a loop body that never executes because its collection is empty; an empty parametrize list; and a benchmark whose fixture measures zero items.
answer: On this worktree 552 of 10201 product pytest tests are tautological. The four catalog controls pass on a scratch copy (assertion-free, uncovered dead-branch assert via sys.settrace, empty-input benchmark caught by len(json.loads(fixture_bytes))=0 not by filename, well-formed negative control including raise AssertionError not flagged). An independent Anthropic-vendor reviewer confirmed 10/10 sampled flagged tests cannot fail. SUCCESS:BLD-0041
method: AST inspection of assert nodes and raise AssertionError (not regex). A live-path raise AssertionError is a real oracle and is not graded NO_ASSERTION. Unreachable asserts are confirmed by executing the test under sys.settrace and observing the assert line uncovered. Empty-input benchmarks are confirmed by loading fixture bytes and counting items at runtime; the fixture file name is never a signal. Retry-policy pivot (regex -> AST) is the shipped method; a comment/string `assert True` is the regex trap.
